abstract_sentences.text: We present protein autoregressive modeling (PAR), the first multi-scale autoregressive framework for protein backbone generation via coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction.
Using the hierarchical nature of proteins, PAR generates structures that mimic sculpting a statue, forming a coarse topology and refining structural details over scales.

evidence.anchor: forming a coarse topology and refining structural details

abstract_sentences.text: To achieve this, PAR consists of three key components: (i) multi-scale downsampling operations that represent protein structures across multiple scales during training; (ii) an autoregressive transformer that encodes multi-scale information and produces conditional embeddings to guide structure generation; (iii) a flow-based backbone decoder that generates backbone atoms conditioned on these embeddings.
Moreover, autoregressive models suffer from exposure bias, caused by the training and the generation procedure mismatch, and substantially degrades structure generation quality.
We effectively alleviate this issue by adopting noisy context learning and scheduled sampling, enabling robust backbone generation.

evidence.anchor: noisy context learning and scheduled sampling

abstract_sentences.text: Notably, PAR exhibits strong zero-shot generalization, supporting flexible human-prompted conditional generation and motif scaffolding without requiring fine-tuning.
On the unconditional generation benchmark, PAR effectively learns protein distributions and produces backbones of high design quality, and exhibits favorable scaling behavior.
Together, these properties establish PAR as a promising framework for protein structure generation.

experimental_design.name: research_questions

experimental_design.name: datasets
experimental_design.description: Curated AFDB representative dataset D_FS has about 0.6M structures, pLDDT > 80, lengths 32–256, and a 98:19:1 train/validation/test split; PDB fine-tuning uses a reproduced 21K designable subset.

experimental_design.name: long_protein_dataset
experimental_design.description: PDB filtering yields 26K designable proteins of lengths 256–768 for a 10K-step fine-tuning analysis.

experimental_design.name: models_and_baselines
experimental_design.description: PAR uses 60M/200M/400M flow decoders and a default 60M AR Transformer; baselines include FrameDiff, RFDiffusion, ESM3, Genie2 and Proteina.

claim_closure.claim: PAR is the first multi-scale autoregressive framework for protein backbone generation.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (1)–(4), multi-scale downsampling, AR Transformer and flow decoder define PAR.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 1–2 and the related-work contrast establish the proposed scope, but “first” depends on the paper’s literature coverage.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 restates the first multi-scale AR framing.

evidence.anchor: To our knowledge, autoregressive modeling has not been widely applied

claim_closure.claim: Continuous Cα decoding avoids discretization loss while multi-scale ordering addresses bidirectional dependencies.
claim_closure.method_response: The Transformer conditions a flow-matching Cα decoder on prior upsampled scales.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 compares mixed baseline families and Table 14 diagnoses spatial relations, but no strict matched token-versus-continuous causal comparison is provided.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 repeats the discretization and unidirectional-dependency motivation.

evidence.anchor: This avoids discretizing protein structures into tokens

claim_closure.claim: NCL and SS mitigate exposure bias and improve generation quality.
claim_closure.method_response: NCL corrupts prior context and SS replaces context with predicted coordinates at probability 0.5.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3 directly compares teacher forcing, NCL and NCL+SS on sc-RMSD, FPSD and fS.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 explicitly lists exposure bias among addressed limitations.

claim_closure.claim: PAR forms coarse topology and refines structural detail progressively.
claim_closure.method_response: Hierarchical downsampling, shared decoder and scale-wise upsampling implement the coarse-to-fine process.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 visualizes samples and Figures 6–10 inspect attention or sampling, but attention is correlational evidence for mechanism.

evidence.anchor: the model first formulates the global structural layout
retains non-negligible attention to earlier scales

claim_closure.claim: PAR captures protein distributions with high design quality.
claim_closure.method_response: The flow decoder and evaluation protocol target both sample quality and distributional fidelity.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 reports designability, FPSD and fS, but some baseline values come from Geffner et al. and PDB fine-tuning data are reconstructed.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 summarizes distributional fidelity and generation quality.

evidence.anchor: Results for the remaining baselines are taken directly

claim_closure.method_response: Decoder size and training-step sweeps are used to test scaling.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5 and Table 13 support a decoder-capacity trend, but no fitted scaling law, seeds or uncertainty is reported.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 mentions powerful distributional fidelity but does not add a new scaling result.

evidence.anchor: Performance of four metrics over varying training steps and model sizes

claim_closure.claim: PAR enables point-prompted conditional generation and motif scaffolding without fine-tuning.
claim_closure.method_response: The first scale can be initialized with a 16-point prompt; motif coordinates are teacher-forced at each scale.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 3–4 and Table 5 support prompt following, while Table 11 shows heterogeneous motif success and a training-condition asymmetry.

claim_closure.claim: Multi-scale orchestration gives a 2.5× sampling speedup relative to a single-scale baseline.
claim_closure.method_response: KV cache and per-scale SDE/ODE schedules reduce expensive fine-scale steps.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 and Table 8 report 67/68 s versus Proteina’s 131/170 s at lengths 150/200; the claim is conditional on the stated hardware, steps and sample count.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 leaves the numerical speed result in the experimental discussion.

claim_closure.claim: The flow-based model is a special case of PAR under one scale.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (1)–(3) reduce the product and context to a single scale.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The reduction is formal; Proteina is used as the single-scale runtime/quality comparator.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 explicitly calls PAR a general framework including flow-based methods.

evidence.anchor: naturally reduces to a flow-based model
offering a general framework that includes flow-based methods

claim_closure.claim: Length-based three-scale configuration is the preferred default.
claim_closure.method_response: Scale sizes are explicit hyperparameters and can be length- or ratio-defined.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 4 compares configurations and supports the reported default choice.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No new configuration claim is added in §5.

evidence.anchor: We adopt this as the default configuration

claim_closure.claim: Sequence downsampling preserves essential pairwise spatial correlations.
claim_closure.method_response: Downsampling interpolates coordinates along sequence dimension.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 14 gives low RMSE and LDDT 1 against an interpolated 2D distance-map comparator; it is a diagnostic, not a downstream causal test.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The claim is not revisited in §5.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 蛋白 backbone 的层级结构提供了比 residue-wise 单向顺序更合适的 AR state；确定性 sequence downsampling 构造 coarse-to-fine scales，AR Transformer 汇总此前 scales，shared flow decoder 在连续 Cα 空间逐 scale 生成，NCL/SS 让推理时的自生成 context 进入训练。[p. 4–6, §3]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留 Eq. (1)–(6)、Figure 1–2、Table 1–5、NCL/SS、主要训练/采样条件、2.5× runtime 和 prompt/motif 案例，使 state、机制和主要 trade-off 可核对。[p. 4–11]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: 评测阈值与分母、数据构造、长蛋白退化、unseen scale、per-token decoder 失败、self-conditioning、Foldseek cluster 和 training time 移入 A–C；不读 C.3/C.5/C.6 会高估能力边界。[p. 16–24]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Eq. (1) 固定 probabilistic decomposition，Figure 1 对齐 training/inference state，Figure 2 显示 coarse-to-fine，Table 3 展示 teacher forcing → NCL → SS，Table 2 成对呈现 runtime/designability。[p. 2–3, 4, 9–10]
final_judgment.largest_gap: zero-shot motif success 高度异质且与 fine-tuned baseline 条件不对称；Table 1 的总体聚合也遮蔽长蛋白退化和 PDB subset 可复现性问题。[p. 7–8, 20–21]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 有 coarse-to-fine state 的生成论文，应在正文以状态图、形式分解、组件消融和成本–质量表分别证明 state、mechanism、capability 和 trade-off，并紧邻披露分母与失败边界。[p. 2, 4–6, 9–11]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于有明确层级状态和可重复指标的生成任务；涉及 sequence/side-chain/all-atom、复杂条件控制或跨源比较时，需要新增状态、匹配基线、seed 与不确定性证据。[p. 12, §5; p. 24, Appendix E]

narrative_chain: context → AR problem/failure → hierarchical multi-scale insight → deterministic decomposition → scale-wise Transformer conditioning → continuous flow decoder → exposure-bias training → unconditional/zero-shot/scaling evidence → scope and future work.
statistics_summary: Reported quantities are point estimates: proportions, means, RMSD, TM-score, FPSD, fS, RMSE, LDDT, runtime and cluster counts. The PDF reports no seeds, uncertainty intervals, hypothesis tests, bootstrap, Bayesian analysis, regression or multiple-comparison correction.
theory_summary: Seven numbered displayed equations (1)–(7) define decomposition, conditioning, flow-matching objective, SDE/ODE sampling and self-conditioning. No theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary or proof appears.
appendix_summary: Appendix spans pages 16–24 and supplies implementation, metrics, datasets, long-protein results, motif benchmark, sampling/scale/size ablations, spatial diagnostics, attention and training time.
